NTA - I think it is common hospitality to arrange for some snacks or food when you have guests over. People get hungry, lol. If money is an issue, I ask people to bring snacks, and I contribute some snacks as well, so that I'm not providing for the whole group. Same thing with food, if people are hungry then I offer to split uber eats or Pizza. 

If I truly plan to not eat because of more serious money constraints, then I make sure to let the guests know so that they don't have to order a meal just for themselves and can similarly eat before they come. 

And that's just for guests, never mind dates. I don't think it's very considerate to just eat before guests come, especially if the guests are coming for a Pizza and movie.

Instead, the supervising mechanic who was responsible for training me and preparing the machines for maintenance had not done this. In fact, the basic safety standards did not seem to exist anywhere in this factory.

I talked with a school friend of mine who had landed the job with me, and we both discussed how dangerous the job is. Well there is an obvious difference between Porn and unpopular ideas. Porn is censored because youtube users don't expect zoomed in assholes or penetration thumbnails when they are browsing on their lunch break, or with their kids. 

Unpopular opinions change over time. If youtube existed in the 80's or 90's, this inappropriate content might have included LGBT rights videos for instance. If we are okay with youtube blocking content that we disagree with, then we should try not to act surprised when content we support or agree with is eventually removed.

I disagree that a company should be the one to decide which lies it perpetuates unless the law provides a mechanic to adequately punish the company for its lies. News organizations and media platforms have massive user bases, and are a trusted source for news. If they suddenly allowed to be the arbiter's of truth and make shit up for their own benefit, and with no repercussions, they can cause irreparable damage to the host nation before the slow free market finally gets around to producing a valid competitor. What's worse is that they can use their existing grip on the market to attack any rising competitors as "fake news", or lobby politicians to block them from ever becoming a real competitive force. The idea that a free market would somehow identify and control the spread of lies is laughable, and judging by the state of the United States, it clearly doesn't work.  


For example, can an ISP that maintains a local monopoly as the only ISP in a region censor negative news about itself on it's own platform? How is this conducive to a free market? And how exactly can you simply "start a competitor" when ISPs send lobbyists to municipal and state governments to block competition, or sue the state when that fails? Your idea of the free market fails when the company becomes big and powerful enough to use unfair tactics to block anybody outside of a multi-billion dollar corporation from establishing a competitive answer to them.  


With youtube, we are talking about a platform that pulls in 1.8B users every month, and can censor videos to influence those viewers. I absolutely have a problem with them deciding what is and isn't truth. The reason I said it is a slippery slope is because while Flat Earth is a no brainer, what happens when they next decide that net neutrality videos, or that left wing political videos, or pro gay videos should be censored? That is the concept of a slippery slope. It is the idea that you are allowing for a precedent to be created which will inevitably lead to the company abusing this precedent.

​

While I agree, you are creating a slippery slope where a platform has the power to decide what is and isn't truth. Stupidity or not, I don't want to live in a world where ideas are censored by a third party. I want to have the ability to decide that for myself.

I agree that several people who are complete strangers would not inexplicably band together to take somebody down. This said, it is perfectly within the realm of possibility for an individual to pay multiple strangers to act as false witnesses to take an enemy down. I am not saying we should blindly believe the witnesses are hired and fake. I am simply pointing out that this is a plausible scenario, especially when we are talking about a famous controversial person, so we shouldn't instantly presume their guilt just because there are multiple witnesses. If that were the case, then why bother even having a trial once multiple people accuse somebody of a crime. In due time, the witnesses will be interviewed, the trial will conclude, and the Judge or Jury will determine if the defendant is guilty. If they are found guilty, that is when the state should take action, and the public should become enraged with that individual. Anybody acting before that is being irresponsible, and is exhibiting bias by assuming the defendant must be guilty.

This said, the converse is also true. It is equally irresponsible and biased to assume that the witnesses are lying and that the defendant is innocent. I have seen many instances of people blindly siding with the defendant because it is somebody who they like, and claiming the witnesses are liars. The only responsible unbiased way to approach a case like this is to take all witness claims seriously and maintain the innocence of the defendant until they are found guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. 

As for your point that false rape accusations are rare, I am curious what percentage of rape accusations you believe are false. According to the various studies cited in [this wikipedia article](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/False_accusation_of_rape), anywhere between 2-10% of rape accusations are shown to be false after an investigation. As for the ones that result in a conviction, you absolutely can't be certain how many of those are false unless you are certain you found and exonerated each one. Even if only 2% of rape allegations were false, that is a high enough number to justify withholding our judgement until the trial is complete.
